before.name: Head, jawline and external landmarks
before.description: An Arctic and subarctic odontocete with a flexible neck, rounded melon and dorsal ridge in place of a fin. The selected adult is cream-white; calves are gray and skin appearance changes with age and molt. Selected external reconstructions are not measured internal anatomy. New selected external lip/jaw opening and inner oral surfaces are shown in the feeding study; internal tissue unions and physiology remain unresolved.

before.name: Horizontal flukes and caudal peduncle
before.description: Selected horizontal flukes articulate dorsoventrally with the posterior body. Planform, excursion, tissue limits and optical response are authored and unmeasured; no computed thrust or hydrodynamic validation.

before.name: Dorsal exterior and species-specific appendages
before.description: Selected fin, ridge or finless dorsal region follows this species account. Flipper proportions and visible marks are selected external comparisons, not universal diagnostics or fitted specimen dimensions.

after.name: Melon, rostrum and soft lips
after.description: Rounded, overhanging forehead and short broad rostrum replace the pointed prior face. The melon contour study gives a selected extension and retraction; this has no fitted tissue-volume, sound-beam or emotion model.

after.name: Horizontal flukes and peduncle
after.description: Broad notched horizontal flukes with a thicker root and narrow vertical peduncle. Span/chord are selected near published beluga cohort proportions; dorsoventral heave and foil pitch are distinct, without a thrust calculation.

after.name: Dorsal ridge and ivory skin
after.description: A low longitudinal ridge replaces a fin. Adult-white skin retains faint mottling, sparse creases and scars with restrained numerical normal/roughness fields; this is no measured reflectance or exact micron-scale skin replica.

after.name: Flexible neck and pectorals
after.description: Cervical blending permits a bounded local head turn while eyes, lips and blowhole follow the head. Short rounded paddle flippers have substantial bases; the shoulder union and cervical limits remain selected, unmeasured approximations.

after.name: Lips, teeth and tongue
after.description: Choose Open mouth and Open mouth in the stage controls to inspect 36 selected worn peg teeth, gingival borders, palate and tongue. Choose feeding to inspect pursing and reduced lateral gape instead. Oral display is not a normal suction-feeding gape or complete swallowing.

after.name: Eye, lids and blowhole
after.description: Small inset lateral dark eyes have soft folded lid rims. A single closed blowhole sits dorsally behind the melon. These exterior landmarks follow neck motion; blinking, respiration and sound production are not simulated.

after.title: Beluga whale · extensively resculpted CC0 control surface
after.author: 3D Assets (CC0 source); PhenoVoxel Archive (MIT additions)

after.biology: Contributor-reported AI-generated static model. Source dimensions are asset authoring units, not biological measurements; no source skeleton, animation or tissue data. New selected adult exterior is reference-led and unvalidated.
changes: Decoded the quantized source control surface without clamping; retained 81 body ring stations, resampled to 161 rings and 96 circumferential segments; changed proportions, forehead, chin, neck, trunk and peduncle.
Replaced simplified source appendages, facial marks and ridge with rounded pectorals, broad horizontal flukes, low dorsal ridge, inset eyes/lids, single blowhole and integrated split lips.

Added a separate selected 36-tooth oral cavity, gums and tongue; exterior pursing and gular depression follow published stage order. No live scan, anatomical dissection, pressure, prey or swallowing solver.
Original ivory/normal/roughness texture fields; no supplied-image pixels. Finite stroke, glide, head turn, melon-contour and feeding studies; no source or independently validated motion.
